summary: This investigative report examines how growing federal and state regulations and compliance demands disproportionately burden small businesses, which lack the resources of large corporations. It uses cases from ecommerce, manufacturing, consulting and restaurants, and covers tax, cybersecurity and licensing challenges. It closes with efforts toward simplification, including the "Cut the Red Tape" campaign and AI-powered compliance tools.
one_line: Small businesses struggle with rising regulatory and compliance burdens across tax, cybersecurity and licensing, prompting calls for simplification and technology-based solutions.
key_facts: On September 15, 2023, the Department of Commerce unveiled guidelines to enhance transparency in online retail operations, adding complexity for small businesses like Alicia Mendez's boutique ecommerce platform.
A Small Business Association survey released October 10, 2023 found small businesses spend an average of 200 hours per year on compliance-related issues, costing roughly $6,000 in labor alone.
On November 5, 2023, a new environmental regulation required all local manufacturers to reduce their carbon output by 10%; Gilberto Ruiz's manufacturing firm had just three months to comply.
Gilberto Ruiz had to hire a consultant that wasn't in his budget to understand the new environmental regulation, since the alternative was risking fines he couldn't afford.
The IRS issued new tax filing guidelines effective January 1, 2024, introducing new reporting categories for small businesses.
Tax professional Helen Webber says "The tax code is a living document," and that small businesses without a tax expert risk errors and missed deductions.
Sophia Toruno, who owns a mid-sized consultancy firm, suffered a data breach exposing client information on September 28, 2023.
The Federal Trade Commission issued its latest cybersecurity framework on December 1, 2023, aimed at bolstering online platforms' defenses; Toruno was left scrambling to understand it.
Restaurateur Thomas Keller (not the famous chef) complained that health codes in the food-service industry "seem to change with the wind."
On February 20, 2024, a coalition led by entrepreneur David Nguyen launched the "Cut the Red Tape" campaign to open dialogue with policymakers on reducing unnecessary bureaucracy.
Proposed solutions include creating a small business liaison office within regulatory bodies to provide guidance and streamline communication.
Anika Singh's startup developed an AI-powered platform that automates much of compliance tracking and reporting for small businesses.
Financial consultant Jeremy Li argues the playing field is not level because small business owners must act as CEO, compliance officer and accountant at once.
